the results of this study do not support the hypothesis that PCIT is more effective for children whose parents report higher numbers of adverse experiences.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the number of ACEs parents reported was associated with their children’s externalising behaviors at baseline, but the association was not significant at post-treatment.

parents with more adverse childhood experiences (e.g., abuse, neglect, household dysfunction) are more likely to have children with more externalizing behaviors (e.g., aggressive behavior, hyperactivity).

The main takeaway from our work is that
parents with four or greater adverse childhood experiences (ACES) are more likely to experience a reduction in child externalizing behaviors following treatment.
parents with more ACEs may benefit from more intensive treatment.
